name: Social proof

pinned_evidence.title: Studies of independence and conformity: A minority of one against a unanimous majority
A focus theory of normative conduct
The Effect of Word of Mouth on Sales

evidence.basis: People use others' behavior as evidence for the correct action, especially under uncertainty (Asch conformity; Cialdini's focus theory of normative conduct). Descriptive norms reliably shift behavior; online reviews measurably affect purchasing.
evidence.effect_size_note: Robust but context-dependent: strongest under uncertainty and when the referent group is similar/relevant. Descriptive norms ('most people do X') move behavior reliably in field studies; magnitude varies by domain.

mechanism_summary_for_context: When unsure, people look to what others do and treat it as evidence of the right choice. Show credible, relevant social signals — real usage numbers, genuine reviews, what similar users chose, 'most popular' — and uncertainty resolves toward the socially-validated option. Signals must be true and the referent should be relevant to the user. Strongest at decision points under uncertainty.

preconditions.reason: requires genuine social data — real users, real reviews, real choices; fabricated social proof is forbidden and ineffective long-term

applicability.culture_note: Social proof is universal but referent norms differ (individualist vs collectivist weighting, which groups count); an L3 surface parameter

implementations.generation_directive: Show genuine, specific social signals: real user counts stated as an actual number, real ratings. Specificity and truth beat vague grandiosity — any such count is shown only if true. Prefer referents similar to the user where the data allows.

Indicate what similar users chose — the option genuinely selected most often by users in the same segment — where genuinely true, to resolve choice uncertainty. Any such popularity label must reflect real selection data, not a marketing preference.

hard_rules.rule: All social-proof signals (counts, ratings, 'most popular', reviews) must be genuine and current; fabricated or inflated social proof is forbidden
No fake 'X people viewing/bought recently' notifications unless literally true and verifiable
Never generate, imply, or display fabricated reviews or testimonials

constraints.boundary_test: Is the social signal true and relevant — or manufactured to fake consensus?

relations.note: Social proof (others as evidence) is distinct from status/comparison (standing relative to others); they co-occur but differ in driver
Demand-caused scarcity ('others want it') borrows social proof; distinct driver (availability vs consensus)

reference_examples.what: Star ratings and review counts as decision evidence — the canonical social-proof interface
Real-time demand signal — effective when true, a regulatory target when fabricated
Credible customer logos resolve B2B uncertainty via relevant-referent social proof
